record.original_question: Does every graph G satisfy the total-coloring bound chi''(G) <= Delta(G) + 2?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 37 ([12, 171, 172]). Every graph G satisfies χ′′(G) 6 ∆ + 2.

Every graph G satisfies χ′′(G) 6 ∆ + 2. This is Conjecture 37, posed independently by Bezhad and by Vizing. Asymptotically, the best result on this problem is that there exists a constant C such that χ′′(G) 6 ∆ + C; see Theorem 38.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G = (V, E)$ be a finite simple graph with maximum degree $\Delta(G)$. A total coloring of $G$ is an assignment of colors to the elements of $V \cup E$ such that: (i) any two adjacent vertices receive different colors, (ii) any two incident edges receive different colors, and (iii) any vertex and any edge incident to it receive different colors. The total chromatic number $\chi''(G)$ is the smallest number of colors for which $G$ admits a total coloring.

Prove or disprove: every finite simple graph $G$ satisfies
$$\chi''(G) \le \Delta(G) + 2.$$
artifact.status_search_result: The Total Coloring Conjecture, posed independently by Behzad (1965) and Vizing (1964), remains open in general. The best known asymptotic result is $\chi''(G) \le \Delta(G) + C$ for some absolute constant $C$ (Molloy–Reed, 1998), and recent work has improved constants, but the conjectured bound $\Delta + 2$ is not established for all graphs.

status_evidence.title: Total coloring - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: It is an open problem whether every graph has a total coloring using at most Δ+2 colors. This is the total coloring conjecture (Behzad 1965; Vizing 1964).
status_evidence.claim: The Total Coloring Conjecture is open.

status_evidence.title: Molloy, Reed: A bound on the total chromatic number
status_evidence.snippet: There exists an absolute constant C such that χ''(G) ≤ Δ(G) + C for every graph G.
status_evidence.claim: Best known asymptotic result toward TCC.
